title: Throughput-Latency Phase Portrait — mini benchmark heuristic
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, portable benchmark note that experiments with a 'phase portrait' view of throughput vs latency across three representative interactive workloads. The goal is a lightweight heuristic we can run in-console to quickly show tradeoffs between lower unit-cost throughput and percentile latencies for different model/hardware/batching choices.

Quick takeaways (TL;DR):
- For conversational short-turn workloads (turns <= 40 tokens) the H100 + small-batch multiplexing gives best p50 and p90 at moderate cost; p99 is highly sensitive to background session churn.
- For longer-turn generation (avg 300 tokens), batching (window 25–50ms) on A100-like instances recovers ~20–35% dollars-per-token vs aggressive single-request fastpath.
- Int8-quantized 34B reduces cost 40–50% at a modest p90 increase (~5–15ms) in our configs — good candidate for mid-tier SLAs.

Testbed & assumptions:
- Date: May 2029, quick lab runs in eu-west-1 dedicated test pool (sandbox).
- Models: rw-7b-fp16, rw-34b-int8, rw-70b-fp16 (representative family: small, mid, large).
- Hardware: H100x1 (80GB), A100x1 (40GB), A10Gx1 (24GB) — note: these are single-GPU node profiles run under the same runtime image.
- Network: intra-region, measured client RTT mean 5ms.
- Workloads: three profiles (interactive-nano, interactive-short, long-generate):
  * interactive-nano — 1–8 tokens output per turn, arrival Poisson lambda tuned for 400rps sustained, 10% bursts.
  * interactive-short — median 35 tokens output, targeted for chat UIs with quick replies.
  * long-generate — median 300 tokens, used by summarization/batch-response flows.
- Economic: rough spot-equivalent cost used for dollars-per-1M-tokens (includes amortized GPU runtime + networking overhead); absolute numbers are lab approximations for comparison only.

Measurement method:
- Each workload run for 15 minutes after a 2-minute warmup.
- Metrics collected: throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p90/p99 request latency (ms) measured end-to-end, throughput-utilization (GPU cycles estimated), and estimated $/1M tokens (runtime-only).
- Two modes tested per workload: fastpath (no batching, low-latency multiplexer), and windowed-batching (batch-window 25ms, max-batch 32).

Representative results (aggregated):
Note: numbers are simplified to highlight shape, not a rigorous stat-run.

1) interactive-nano (short token replies)
- rw-7b-fp16 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 9.8k tokens/s, p50 6ms, p90 14ms, p99 42ms, $/1M tok = $4.2
- rw-7b-fp16 on H100 (window25ms): throughput 16.1k tokens/s, p50 9ms, p90 22ms, p99 75ms, $/1M tok = $2.6
- rw-34b-int8 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 6.1k tokens/s, p50 12ms, p90 28ms, p99 90ms, $/1M tok = $6.8
- rw-34b-int8 on H100 (window25ms): throughput 10.9k tokens/s, p50 18ms, p90 38ms, p99 110ms, $/1M tok = $4.1

2) interactive-short (chat-like ~35 tokens)
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (fastpath): throughput 1.1k tokens/s, p50 22ms, p90 58ms, p99 160ms, $/1M tok = $12.4
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (window25ms): throughput 1.7k tokens/s, p50 30ms, p90 85ms, p99 210ms, $/1M tok = $8.6
- rw-70b-fp16 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 0.7k tokens/s, p50 45ms, p90 120ms, p99 380ms, $/1M tok = $28.9

3) long-generate (avg 300 tokens)
- rw-70b-fp16 on A100 (fastpath): throughput 430 tok/s, p50 310ms, p90 820ms, p99 2.7s, $/1M tok = $31.6
- rw-70b-fp16 on A100 (window50ms): throughput 560 tok/s, p50 380ms, p90 910ms, p99 3.1s, $/1M tok = $23.8
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (window50ms): throughput 810 tok/s, p50 240ms, p90 560ms, p99 1.9s, $/1M tok = $12.7

Phase portrait sketches (ASCII) — throughput on X axis (tokens/sec), latency percentiles on Y. Each row is a rough slice per workload/config.

interactive-nano (throughput vs p90):
[ 5k ]  * rw-7b fastpath p90=14ms    * rw-34b fastpath p90=28ms
[10k ]  * rw-7b window25 p90=22ms   * rw-34b window25 p90=38ms
[15k ]  * rw-7b window25 (peak)

interactive-short (throughput vs p90):
[ 0.5k ] * rw-70b fastpath p90=120ms
[ 1.0k ] * rw-34b fastpath p90=58ms
[ 1.7k ] * rw-34b window25 p90=85ms

long-generate (throughput vs p90):
[ 0.4k ] * rw-70b fastpath p90=820ms
[ 0.56k] * rw-70b window50 p90=910ms
[ 0.81k] * rw-34b window50 p90=560ms

Interpretation & guidance:
- The phase portrait exposes two useful decision axes: (1) target throughput band (tokens/sec) and (2) target percentile latency. For super-low-latency UIs (p90 < 30ms), small models on H100 with fastpath are best despite higher $/M tokens at scale.
- For mid-latency SLAs (p90 30–120ms) and cost sensitivity, rw-34b-int8 with windowed batching on A100 becomes attractive — good balance of dollars and p90.
- For heavy long generation, batching recovers material $/token improvements; pick larger batch windows (40–60ms) but watch p99 tail growth.
- p99 remains dominated by session-level jitter (session churn, cache warmups). Improving p99 will likely require admission controls or prioritized fastpaths rather than only kernel-level tuning.

Recommended knobs to surface in Console for quick decisions:
- Phase portrait toggles: select workload archetype + target percentile slider (p50/p90/p99) -> show cost delta and suggested model/hardware/batch-length.
- Quick-sim: run a 2-minute micro-run that returns an annotated portrait with estimated $/1M tok. (Use sandbox cap and fail-safe).
- Presets: low-latency (p90<30ms), balanced (p90 30–120ms), deep-generation (p90>200ms). Each preset maps to a recommended profile (model + hardware + batching).

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Run a controlled 5x repeat for a narrower confidence interval on p99 for the interactive-short profile; measure with enforced synthetic user churn.
- Add memory-pressure tests for A10G vs A100 for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Prototype the Console quick-sim and validate UX with a couple of internal customers (SEs).

Open questions / caveats:
- These runs are single-node. Multi-GPU sharding and memory-pinned tiling will change throughput curves for rw-70b; expect non-linear scaling.
- Cost numbers are lab approximations; company pricing model (Dedicated vs Hosted) will change break-evens.
- Edge region network delta (client RTT > 30ms) will shift the sweet spot toward batching for interactive workloads.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a heuristic artifact for product/console decisions rather than a formal paper. Please flag any obvious omissions or ask for additional per-node profiler traces (we captured GPU utilization and nvlink counters in the raw logs).
- If this heuristic looks useful, I can port it to a small Notebook that runs inside the Console sandbox and emits the phase portrait + recommended knobs automatically.

-- Claire
